cells.name: Continuity and responsiveness
cells.example: T4-T6 each name a prior speaker's position before answering it.
cells.limitation: T2 ignores T1's testing method; T3 repeats T1's 'stop all three' without engaging.

cells.name: Development of ideas
cells.example: T6 adds 'your skin has no backup' as a reason against face testing.
cells.limitation: No later turn adds a new distinction; T7 and T10 only adjust waiting times.

cells.name: Exploration of central tensions
cells.example: T4 vs T5: waste of discarding vs time lost in pain.
cells.limitation: Patch testing off the face, active ingredients, irritation vs allergy never raised by any mind.

cells.name: Integration of perspectives
cells.example: T10 Tester lengthens the pause in response to the Risk Analyst.
cells.limitation: Tester simply yields (T7, T10); views do not reshape each other's reasoning.

cells.name: Progress toward understanding
cells.example: Section E sets three conditional branches for resuming products.
cells.limitation: T12 ends on product claims vs safety, not on how to find the irritant.

cells.name: Faithful engagement
cells.example: T6 accurately states the Tester's case as controlled testing.
cells.limitation: T4 recasts T2's 'keep only the essentials' as 'discarding everything'.

cells.name: Substance of challenges
cells.example: T6: testing on the face is a poor bet since skin has no backup.
cells.limitation: T6 assumption (face is the only test site) never named; T7 concedes instead of answering.

cells.name: Accuracy and support
cells.example: T1 reintroduction one at a time is a sound elimination method.
cells.limitation: T9 'week of irritation could be a month of recovery' unsupported; T1 quote wording suspected inexact.

cells.name: Calibration and transparency
cells.example: Section E separates branches by skin state.
cells.limitation: Hedges everywhere blur fact and guess; Section D asserts testing 'likely reckless' without basis.

cells.name: Intellectual honesty and revision
cells.example: T7 Tester concedes face testing is risky.
cells.limitation: T7 and T10 concede by restating T6, without narrowing the claim or answering it.

cells.name: Identification of the actual concern
cells.example: Section A frames the need: identify the irritant and soothe the sting.
cells.limitation: T8 and T12 drift to values questions the user never raised.

cells.name: Meaningful use of personal context
cells.example: T1 and T3 act on 'three products' by stopping all three.
cells.limitation: Started 'last week' simultaneously never shapes the argument beyond that.

cells.name: Fit with goals and values
cells.example: T1 targets the user's stated goal of finding the cause.
cells.limitation: T12 substitutes 'product claims vs barrier safety' for the user's diagnostic goal.

cells.name: Attention to constraints and stakes
cells.example: T5 weighs time lost while the face is in pain.
cells.limitation: T6 'rash' and Section E 'breaking out' assume symptoms the user did not report.

cells.name: Responsiveness to information
cells.example: Section E branches on whether skin is inflamed.
cells.limitation: Which products, their actives, sting severity and allergy history never asked or branched.

cells.name: Clarification of desires and motivations
cells.example: T8 offers clear complexion vs simple routine with a question.
cells.limitation: T2 and T5 guess motives ('overwhelmed', 'feel good today') with no answerable question.

cells.name: Examination of assumptions
cells.example: T4 questions the assumption that all products are bad.
cells.limitation: Assumption of a single culprit vs a combination reaction never examined.

cells.name: Clarification of values and priorities
cells.example: T8 asks which matters more: complexion or simple routine.
cells.limitation: Values are imported rather than drawn from the user's question (T8, T12).

cells.name: Recognition of fears and outside expectations
cells.example: T9 names fear of looking worse if products stop.
cells.limitation: Only one fear surfaced; T2 'overwhelmed' is an unprompted guess.

cells.name: Agency and reflective ownership
cells.example: T8 and T9 end with questions the user can answer.
cells.limitation: Questions concern priorities, not the user's own observations of the reaction.

cells.name: Definition of the decision and options
cells.example: Options span stop all, discard, sequential testing, waiting, dermatologist.
cells.limitation: Patch test on arm or jawline, the standard limited step, never offered.

cells.name: Explanation of tradeoffs
cells.example: T4 waste of discarding vs T5 time in pain.
cells.limitation: Cost of losing a product that was fine (T2 discard) left unweighed.

cells.name: Identification of decisive conditions
cells.example: Section E: if skin is inflamed, stop all products.
cells.limitation: No observable sign separating irritation from allergy; four days, one week ungrounded.

cells.name: Treatment of uncertainty
cells.example: Section E flags uncertainty about skin damage.
cells.limitation: Ingredient identity, the most consequential unknown, never separated from minor ones.

cells.name: Proportionate next steps
cells.example: T10: pause one week, then one product for three days.
cells.limitation: Timeframes conflict across T1, T7, T10; no warning signs prompting urgent care.

cells.name: Accessible language
cells.example: T6 'your skin has no backup' is plain and concrete.
cells.limitation: Section E 'skin barrier' and 'fragility' used without explanation.

cells.name: Traceable arguments and references
cells.example: T4-T6 name the mind they answer.
cells.limitation: T12 'we still disagree' on reintroduction, a point no turn argued.

cells.name: Manageable pacing and turn length
cells.example: Twelve short turns, easy to scan.
cells.limitation: T7 falls under 25 words per deterministic check.

cells.name: Distinguishable positions and voices
cells.example: Three distinct stances: test, discard, protect.
cells.limitation: All three minds hedge with 'you might' in nearly every turn.

cells.name: Economy and sustained attention
cells.example: Turns are brief without padding.
cells.limitation: T4-T6 open by recapping the prior speaker; T3 repeats T1's stop advice.

cells.name: Meaningful stakes and tension
cells.example: T6 frames a rash as the downside of face testing.
cells.limitation: Minds largely agree to stop everything; tension stays low.

cells.name: Surprise and reversals
cells.example: T10 Tester drops immediate testing.
cells.limitation: T7 and T10 reversals restate T6 without naming a new argument.

cells.name: Personality and expressive voice
cells.example: T1 Bacon's candle line gives the Tester some colour.
cells.limitation: Minimalist and Risk Analyst lack Kondo's or Taleb's voice; shared hedging register.

cells.name: Memorable delivery
cells.example: T6 'your skin has no backup' lands.
cells.limitation: Few images beyond T1 and T6; T11 and T12 are flat.

cells.name: Anticipation and emotional movement
cells.example: T9 raises cost from a week to a month.
cells.limitation: Uniform turn length and tone throughout; no build or release.

strengths: T1 proposes a workable stop-then-reintroduce method aimed at the user's actual question.
T6 Risk Analyst gives a concrete objection: the face has no backup.
Section E offers conditional branches including a dermatologist route.
weaknesses: No mind raises patch testing elsewhere, active ingredients, or allergy vs irritation (T1-T12).
Never asks which products or how severe the sting is (whole debate).
Tester concedes in T7 and T10 without answering T6; hedged uniform voice across minds.

symptoms.observed: Face-testing objection conceded; testing on a small patch elsewhere never raised.
symptoms.evidence: Testing on your own face is a poor bet

symptoms.observed: No turn asks which products or actives, or how severe the stinging is.
symptoms.evidence: stop all three products now, then reintroduce one every four days

symptoms.observed: Tester concedes by restating the opponent, no narrowed claim or answer.
symptoms.evidence: I concede that testing on your face is risky.

symptoms.observed: Diagnostic question turned into a values question the user never raised.
symptoms.evidence: value the product claims more than the safety

symptoms.observed: All minds hedge with 'might/maybe/perhaps'; voices merge.
symptoms.evidence: You might be treating your face like a lab

findings.description: Turn 7 is 23 words, under the 25-word floor (deterministic check reports one turn under range).
Bacon quotation (Novum Organum I.82) commonly rendered 'first lights the candle'; 'kindles' wording and translation unnamed.
Claim that a week of irritation could mean a month of recovery has no stated basis.
No mention of signs warranting prompt medical care (swelling, hives, blistering); dermatologist only if unsure.
States immediate testing is likely reckless, though the debate never weighed off-face patch testing.

rubric_fit_notes: Troubleshooting question labelled decision; criterion 4 has limited natural scope for a skincare reaction, so C4 ratings reflect thin but not absent opportunity. Bacon quotation judged from memory only.
question_type_note: Read as a decision (troubleshooting) question: options, conditions and next steps judged on how well they identify the irritant safely.
